answer: Persistent reputation dividend with retroactive dilution. Each identity accrues a dividend stream from a shared pool, but the pool inlet is fixed per epoch. Cloning splits that stream across more identities, so a clone syndicate earns less per identity than a single honest actor would have. An attacker who chooses to wander across many fresh keys pays full registration compute plus lost dividend history at each hop. To forge a credible history, they must sustain real activity costs longer than the clone earns back, making honesty the cheaper path.
